text.p: Italian bond futures started a touch firmer but soon slipped back on some scattered profit-taking in early trading after the strong run-up in the market seen on Wednesday, dealers said.

However, the BTP market continued to be supported by talk of a possible interest rate cut by the Bank of Italy which may come next week after preliminary May CPI data. These figures are expected to show a further fall in the annual rate from April.
The lira continued to hold firm despite some softness from the dollar, and this added to the view that the Bank of Italy has a good window of opportunity to cut interest rates.

Data showing Italy industrial production in March declined 3.6 percent year-on-year had little overall impact, although some dealers said the weakness of the Italian economy strengthened the case for an interest rate cut.

Dealers said that the early weakness in German bunds undermined Wednesday's strong BTP rally, but the mood on the Italian market was still positive and most had eyes on preliminary May CPI inflation data due out next week.
"Talk of an interest rate cut on the back of good CPI numbers will continue to give the market good support into next week," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said that the higher T-bond close overnight on the back of a 0.6 percent drop in April U.S. PPI had given the market support, and BTP were likely to try and push firmer again later in the day.
